items.followUp: A pump lifts 50 kg of water through a vertical height of 12 m in 8 s. Calculate its power in watts and horsepower. (Take g = 10 m/s² and 1 hp = 746 W.)

rubric.why: These identify the given SI data and the relation between power and gravitational work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the given mass, height, and time together with P = mgh/t.

rubric.why: The substitution and calculated result show the power in watts.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct substitution and answer with unit.

rubric.why: This is the conversion needed to express power in horsepower.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using 1 hp = 746 W.

rubric.why: The answer converts the calculated power to horsepower.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 70 kg, h = 16 m, t = 10 s, g = 10 m/s².
Formula: P = work done / time = mgh/t.
Substitution: P = (70 kg × 10 m/s² × 16 m) / 10 s.
Since 1 hp = 746 W, power in hp = 1120 W / 746 W ≈ 1.50 hp.

items.followUp: What are fundamental quantities and fundamental units? Give one example of each.

rubric.why: A derived quantity is obtained by mathematically combining fundamental quantities; velocity is an example.
rubric.description: Meaning and example of a derived quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining derived quantities as combinations of fundamental quantities and giving a valid example.

rubric.why: A derived unit is obtained by combining fundamental units; m/s is the unit of velocity.
rubric.description: Meaning and example of a derived unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining derived units as combinations of fundamental units and giving a valid example.

modelAnswer: Derived quantities are physical quantities obtained by mathematically combining fundamental quantities; for example, velocity = distance/time.
Derived units are units obtained by combining fundamental units; for example, the unit of velocity is m/s.

items.followUp: State the first condition for equilibrium and write its mathematical equation.

rubric.why: The second condition states that clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance.
rubric.description: Statement of the second condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the total clockwise moments equal the total anticlockwise moments.

accept: sum of clockwise moments=sum of anticlockwise moments
rubric.why: The equation expresses the balance of moments mathematically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation, such as Στ = 0 or clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments.

modelAnswer: The second condition for equilibrium is that the sum of the clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about that point.
Mathematically: Σ(clockwise moments) = Σ(anticlockwise moments), or Στ = 0.
